result.markdown: --- title: "[vals.fmt_partsper()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format values as parts-per quantities. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/blob/main/great_tables/_formats_vals.py#L857-L987){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vals.fmt_partsper( x, to_units="per-mille", symbol="auto", decimals=2, drop_trailing_zeros=False, drop_trailing_dec_mark=True, scale_values=True, use_seps=True, pattern="{x}", sep_mark=",", dec_mark=".", force_sign=False, incl_space="auto", locale=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} With numeric values in a list, we can format the values so that they are rendered as parts-per quantities (per mille, ppm, ppb, etc.). The following keywords are available for the `to_units` parameter: - `"per-mille"`: Per mille (1 part in 1,000) - `"per-myriad"`: Per myriad (1 part in 10,000) - `"pcm"`: Per cent mille (1 part in 100,000) - `"ppm"`: Parts per million (1 part in 1,000,000) - `"ppb"`: Parts per billion (1 part in 1,000,000,000) - `"ppt"`: Parts per trillion (1 part in 1,000,000,000,000) - `"ppq"`: Parts per quadrillion (1 part in 1,000,000,000,000,000) ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [X]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of values to be formatted. [to_units]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["per-mille"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A keyword that signifies the desired output quantity. This can be any from the following set: `"per-mille"`, `"per-myriad"`, `"pcm"`, `"ppm"`, `"ppb"`, `"ppt"`, or `"ppq"`. [symbol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["auto"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The symbol/units to use for the quantity. By default, this is set to `"auto"` and the appropriate symbol will be chosen based on the `to_units` keyword. This can be changed by supplying a string (e.g., using `symbol="ppbV"` when `to_units="ppb"`). [decimals]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The `decimals` values corresponds to the exact number of decimal places to use. A value such as `2.34` can, for example, be formatted with `0` decimal places and it would result in `"2"`. With `4` decimal places, the formatted value becomes `"2.3400"`. The trailing zeros can be removed with `drop_trailing_zeros=True`. [drop_trailing_zeros]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A boolean value that allows for removal of trailing zeros (those redundant zeros after the decimal mark). [drop_trailing_dec_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A boolean value that determines whether decimal marks should always appear even if there are no decimal digits to display after formatting (e.g., `23` becomes `23.` if `False`). By default trailing decimal marks are not shown. [scale_values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should the values be scaled through multiplication according to the keyword set in `to_units`? By default this is `True` since the expectation is that normally values are proportions. Setting to `False` signifies that the values are already scaled and require only the appropriate symbol/units when formatted. [use_seps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The `use_seps` option allows for the use of digit group separators. The type of digit group separator is set by `sep_mark` and overridden if a locale ID is provided to `locale`. This setting is `True` by default. [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["{x}"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A formatting pattern that allows for decoration of the formatted value. The formatted value is represented by the `{x}` (which can be used multiple times, if needed) and all other characters will be interpreted as string literals. [sep_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[","]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The string to use as a separator between groups of digits. For example, using `sep_mark=","` with a value of `1000` would result in a formatted value of `"1,000"`. This argument is ignored if a `locale` is supplied (i.e., is not `None`). [dec_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["."]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The string to be used as the decimal mark. For example, using `dec_mark=","` with the value `0.152` would result in a formatted value of `"0,152"`). This argument is ignored if a `locale` is supplied (i.e., is not `None`). [force_sign]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should the positive sign be shown for positive values (effectively showing a sign for all values except zero)? If so, use `True` for this option. The default is `False`, where only negative numbers will display a minus sign. [incl_space]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["auto"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : An option for whether to include a space between the value and the symbol/units. The default is `"auto"` which provides spacing dependent on the mark itself (symbols like `‰` get no space; text abbreviations like `ppm` get a space). This can be directly controlled by using either `True` or `False`. [locale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional locale identifier that can be used for formatting values according the locale's rules. Examples include `"en"` for English (United States) and `"fr"` for French (France). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of formatted values is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e48d25be .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_partsper([0.001, 0.0001], to_units="per-mille") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1.00‰', '0.10‰'] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#60a2c4f7 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_partsper([0.0000015, 0.00035], to_units="ppm") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['1.50 ppm', '350.00 ppm'] ``` ::: :::
